info.title: FDDT — Fraud Document Detection Tool API
info.description: FDDT (Fraud Document Detection Tool) backend. Environment: local.

post.summary: Log in and obtain a JWT
post.description: Exchanges email + password for a bearer token (HS256; lifetime from JWT_ACCESS_TOKEN_EXPIRE_MINUTES). The token carries `role`, `company_id` (null for a platform admin) and `is_platform_admin`. An unknown email, a wrong password, a deactivated account and a suspended company all return the same 401 so accounts cannot be enumerated. Throttled (app/services/login_throttle.py): after LOGIN_MAX_FAILED_ATTEMPTS failures an email address is refused for LOGIN_LOCKOUT_MINUTES, and each client IP gets LOGIN_MAX_ATTEMPTS_PER_IP_PER_MINUTE attempts per minute; both answer 429 with a Retry-After header.

429.description: Too many sign-in attempts for this email address or from this IP.

post.description: Any signed-in user (every role) changes their own password by giving the current one. The new password (8-128 characters, different from the current one) is stored hashed and the change is recorded in the audit log (never the password). A forgotten password cannot be reset here: a platform admin resets it (`POST /settings/users/{id}/reset-password`). Tokens already issued stay valid until they expire.

post.description: Opens an empty case (status `submitted`) owned by the caller, in the caller's company; any company role may create one (platform admins may not — 403). The case number is `CASE-` plus the first 8 hex characters of the case UUID. Attach documents afterwards with POST /cases/{case_id}/documents. Writes a `case_created` audit event.

get.description: Only the caller's company. Reviewers see every case of their company; a `user` sees only the cases they submitted. A platform admin must pass `company_id` (one company at a time, audited) — there is no cross-company case list. For `reviewer_l2` and platform admins, open cases escalated to L2 sort first; otherwise newest first. Optional filters: `status`, `case_type`, `assigned_tier`, and `actionable=true` (only cases the caller may act on — for a `reviewer_l1` that excludes L2 cases). Each item carries `can_act`. For submitters `risk_tier` is null and `flag` is a neutral 'In review' marker, so scoring signals are never disclosed to them.

post.summary: Upload a document to a case
post.description: One file per request (multipart field `file`). The original bytes are stored immutably in Blob Storage at `companies/{company_id}/cases/{case_id}/documents/{document_id}_{sha256}{ext}`, a `documents` row is written with the file's SHA-256, then the Celery pipeline is enqueued (extraction, metadata forensics, ELA/copy-move, duplicate detection, visual review, signature detection). The response returns immediately with `processing_status: pending`; poll GET /cases/{case_id} for progress. Before anything is stored or queued the file is validated: at most the company's per-file limit (`max_file_size_mb`, set by a platform admin; 10 MB by default), not empty, a PDF by its header bytes (not its name), a matching extension, and locally parseable (not corrupted, not password-protected). A rejection returns `detail: {code, message, ...}` with one of the codes `file_empty`, `file_too_large`, `unsupported_file_type`, `file_type_mismatch`, `file_corrupted`, `file_password_protected`. Each pipeline step is its own task on a shared, FIFO queue (see app/tasks/celery_app.py). A `user` may upload only to a case they submitted; reviewers to any case of their company; platform admins never (403).

post.summary: Bulk upload: a zip of cases
post.description: Request body: the zip file itself (`Content-Type: application/zip`), not multipart. Query: `case_type` (applied to every case) and `filename` (the zip's name, for display). The zip holds one top-level folder per case, each containing that case's documents directly. The response (202) returns once the zip is stored: it lists every case folder found, with structural failures already marked (subfolder in a case folder, empty folder, empty or file over the company's per-file limit). Documents are then extracted, validated with the same checks as a single upload, and each valid case is created and queued, one case at a time. Poll GET /bulk-uploads/{id}. Partial success: a bad file is rejected on its own and a case with no valid file fails on its own. Zip rejections return `detail: {code, message, ...}` with `zip_empty`, `zip_too_large` (over the company's zip limit, `max_zip_size_mb`, 300 MB by default, decided from Content-Length before the body is read), `not_a_zip`, `zip_corrupted`, `zip_too_many_entries` or `zip_no_case_folders`.

AuditLogEntrySchema.title: AuditLogEntrySchema
AuditLogEntrySchema.description:
One `audit_log` row scoped to a case — System Specification section 3.5's
"review history/timeline ... built from the same audit log." Every
event_type here is a real one already written by app/services/
audit_service.py's call sites (case creation, uploads, and each
Celery check task) — nothing here is synthesized for display.

BoundingBoxSchema.title: BoundingBoxSchema
BoundingBoxSchema.description:
Normalized bounding box — page-fraction (0-1) coordinates, same
convention as every other bounding box in this codebase (ELA, copy-move,
visual inconsistency). `page` is 1-based.

actor_role.title: Actor Role
actor_role.description: Display label of the actor's role when they acted, e.g. 'Reviewer L1'.

CaseActionSchema.title: CaseActionSchema
CaseActionSchema.description: A reviewer decision/note on the case (approve/reject/escalate).

case_type.description: Case-level category chosen at submission. Independent of each document's own `document_type`, which the classification step fills in later.

can_act.title: Can Act
can_act.description: Whether the caller may approve/reject/escalate this case given its tier. False for submitters, and for a `reviewer_l1` on an L2-assigned case (read-only). Does not reflect status — a decided case is still `can_act` but every action is a 409.

CaseDocumentSummary.title: CaseDocumentSummary
CaseDocumentSummary.description:
A document as shown on the case-detail page. `file_url` here is a
short-lived signed URL (see StorageService.get_download_url) — the
storage container is private, so the durable URL alone isn't
browser-fetchable.

`document_type` and `extracted_fields` are filled in by the OCR +
classification + extraction Celery pipeline (app/tasks/document_
processing.py) — both stay null until `processing_status` reaches
"complete". `extracted_fields` shape: {"document_type_confidence":
float, "core_fields": {name: {value, confidence, uncertain}},
"additional_fields": [{field_name, value, confidence, uncertain}]}.

`checks` is filled in afterward by app/tasks/document_checks.py
(field_validation, issuer_verification, and later the forensic
checks) — empty until those complete.

CaseFlagSchema.title: CaseFlagSchema
CaseFlagSchema.description:
Wire shape of app/services/case_flag_service.py's CaseFlag: the
case's real risk tier (low/medium/high), or "pending" until scored.

can_act.title: Can Act
can_act.description: Whether the caller may approve/reject/escalate this case given its tier. False for submitters, and for a `reviewer_l1` on an L2-assigned case (read-only). Does not reflect status — a decided case is still `can_act` but every action is a 409.

CaseReportResponse.title: CaseReportResponse
CaseReportResponse.description:
One generated report. `download_url` is a short-lived signed URL (the
container is private — see app/services/storage_service.py), so it is
minted fresh on every response rather than stored.

CaseTier.title: CaseTier
CaseTier.description:
Which reviewer tier owns the case — orthogonal to `status`. Every case
starts at `l1`; escalating it moves it to `l2` (one-directional, there is
no de-escalation). On an `l2` case a `reviewer_l1` keeps read access but
every action endpoint returns 403; `reviewer_l2` and `admin` can act on
cases of either tier.

CaseType.title: CaseType
CaseType.description:
Case-level category, selected at submission time (System Specification section
3.6's document-type coverage list). This is separate from a document's
own `document_type`, which is filled in later by the classification
step — a case can hold documents of more than one type (e.g. an
invoice plus its approval voucher).

ChangePasswordRequest.title: ChangePasswordRequest
ChangePasswordRequest.description:
Change your own password. The current password is required; a
forgotten password is reset by a platform admin instead (there is no
self-service reset).

max_file_size_mb.title: Max File Size Mb
max_file_size_mb.description: Max document size in MB (per company).

max_zip_size_mb.title: Max Zip Size Mb
max_zip_size_mb.description: Max bulk-upload zip size in MB (per company).

max_file_size_mb.title: Max File Size Mb
max_file_size_mb.description: Largest document this company may upload, in MB.

max_zip_size_mb.title: Max Zip Size Mb
max_zip_size_mb.description: Largest bulk-upload zip this company may upload, in MB.

max_file_size_mb.title: Max File Size Mb
max_file_size_mb.description: Max document size in MB (per company).

max_zip_size_mb.title: Max Zip Size Mb
max_zip_size_mb.description: Max bulk-upload zip size in MB (per company).

CrossDocumentFindingSummary.title: CrossDocumentFindingSummary
CrossDocumentFindingSummary.description:
One `cross_document_findings` row (System Specification section 3.1,
"Cross-document validation & reconciliation") — a shared field
(amount/date/issuer) that disagreed between two of this case's
documents. Case-level, not per-document — see app/services/
cross_document_service.py and app/tasks/document_checks.py.

full_name.title: Full Name
full_name.description: Display name, if one was set.

is_active.title: Is Active
is_active.description: Deactivated accounts are rejected on every request.

is_platform_admin.title: Is Platform Admin
is_platform_admin.description: True for platform admins, who belong to no company.

company_id.title: Company Id
company_id.description: The user's company; null for a platform admin.

company_name.title: Company Name
company_name.description: Display name of the user's company.

DocumentCheckSummary.title: DocumentCheckSummary
DocumentCheckSummary.description:
One `document_checks` row (System Specification sections 2.2/3.1/3.2 —
field_validation, issuer_verification, and later the forensic checks).
`result` holds whatever shape that check_type produces — see the
individual check services (e.g. app/services/field_validation_service.py)
for what's inside — the frontend's Checks panel renders it generically
rather than assuming a fixed schema per check_type.

DocumentFileUrlResponse.title: DocumentFileUrlResponse
DocumentFileUrlResponse.description: A fresh short-lived signed URL for one document's original file.

reason.title: Reason
reason.description: Why the case needs an L2 reviewer. Required and must not be blank.

ForensicFindingSummary.title: ForensicFindingSummary
ForensicFindingSummary.description:
One medium/high-severity finding from a flagged metadata_forensics/
error_level_analysis/copy_move_detection check — the per-document
counterpart to CrossDocumentFindingSummary, both shown together in
the case detail "Explainable findings" panel. See app/services/
case_flag_service.py's get_forensic_findings for what feeds this and
why it's a temporary stand-in for the real risk-scoring engine.

name_arabic.title: Name Arabic
name_arabic.description: Arabic-script name, matched separately during issuer verification.

PipelineStatusSchema.title: PipelineStatusSchema
PipelineStatusSchema.description:
Whether every automated check has finished. `pending` names what is
still outstanding — shown to the reviewer when Approve is disabled.

reason.title: Reason
reason.description: Why the case is rejected. Required and must not be blank.

RiskReasonSchema.title: RiskReasonSchema
RiskReasonSchema.description:
One fired rule, as frozen at scoring time (rendered text, weight and
rule version) — see app/models/case_risk_assessment.py.

rule_id.title: Rule Id
rule_id.description: Stable key, lower-case with a dot: e.g. custom.editing_tool_seen

RiskRuleCreate.title: RiskRuleCreate
RiskRuleCreate.description:
A brand-new rule (version 1). The admin picks a rule TYPE and its
parameters from the catalog (GET /settings/risk-rule-options); the API
builds and validates the engine `condition` from them — nobody writes
JSON, and a choice the engine can't evaluate is rejected.

RiskRuleResponse.title: RiskRuleResponse
RiskRuleResponse.description: One (current or historical) version of a rule.

weight.title: Weight
weight.description: Points added to the case score when the rule fires.

severity.title: Severity
severity.description: Severity shown beside the rule's reason.

is_active.title: Is Active
is_active.description: Inactive rules are evaluated but never fire.

RiskRuleUpdate.title: RiskRuleUpdate
RiskRuleUpdate.description: An edit. Never mutates the existing row: the API inserts version+1.

medium_threshold.title: Medium Threshold
medium_threshold.description: Score at or above which a case is `medium` risk.

high_threshold.title: High Threshold
high_threshold.description: Score at or above which a case is `high` risk. Must exceed the medium threshold.

metadata_score_cap.title: Metadata Score Cap
metadata_score_cap.description: Most points the metadata rules (`metadata.*`) may add together — one edit leaves several metadata traces. 100 = no cap. Omitted: unchanged.

medium_threshold.title: Medium Threshold
medium_threshold.description: Score at or above which a case is `medium` risk.

high_threshold.title: High Threshold
high_threshold.description: Score at or above which a case is `high` risk. Must exceed the medium threshold.

SignatureMatchResponse.title: SignatureMatchResponse
SignatureMatchResponse.description:
One signature_matches row returned by the API, enriched with the
reference's person_name so the frontend can show "compared against [name]"
without a separate reference lookup.

person_name.title: Person Name
person_name.description: Name of the person whose signature this is, typed by the reviewer. Required — the system does not attempt to auto-extract this field.

is_library.title: Is Library
is_library.description: Defaults to True: every reference is saved to the permanent signature library. False is still accepted (case-only reference). Either way, at this phase a reference is only compared against other documents in its own case — no cross-case/library-wide comparison logic runs yet.

SignatureReferenceCreate.title: SignatureReferenceCreate
SignatureReferenceCreate.description:
Request body for POST /cases/{case_id}/documents/{document_id}/
signature-references.

`person_name` is required and must be provided by the reviewer —
the system never attempts to auto-extract or pre-fill it (System Specification §2.3).

SignatureReferenceResponse.title: SignatureReferenceResponse
SignatureReferenceResponse.description: One signature_references row returned by the API.

max_file_size_mb.title: Max File Size Mb
max_file_size_mb.description: Largest document, in MB (1 MB = 1,048,576 bytes).

UploadLimitsResponse.title: UploadLimitsResponse
UploadLimitsResponse.description: The calling company's upload limits, as enforced on its next upload.

start.title: Start
start.description: First UTC day included (null = from the beginning).

end.title: End
end.description: Last UTC day included (null = up to today).

role.description: New role. Cannot be changed on your own account.

company_id.title: Company Id
company_id.description: Move the user to another company (company roles only).

is_active.title: Is Active
is_active.description: False deactivates the account. Not allowed on yourself.

email.title: Email
email.description: Login email. Unique regardless of letter case.

company_id.title: Company Id
company_id.description: Required for company roles; must be empty for `platform_admin`.

UserCreate.title: UserCreate
UserCreate.description:
An account created by an administrator (there is no self-service
sign-up). The password is set here and only ever stored hashed.
